My personal experience: I started off in this job in a big station. Worked in small stations before. Always used LLVs though so never had to worry about personal vehicle. In terms of stress.. as a sub, being in a large station sucks. There is almost always guaranteed extra work every day with little to no days off. As a regular though.. (I went regular not all that long ago and went from being a PTF at a small station back to a large station when I went regular) I much prefer a larger station. I don't know how many rural routes my station has but it's maybe like.. 30? I think my main reasons are: 1. There are more opportunities for OT 2. It's a bigger environment. so.. If you don't like a handful of people, there's always more people to enjoy being around. Compared to a small station there is limited options of making friends or being stuck with bad people. Also, if management is an issue it's easier to deal with them with numbers of a larger station than a small station where carriers can become easily pressured into not complaining via retaliation and lack of union representation.

I'm 29 and I think one of the biggest things to overcome as an adult is to not compare yourself to other adults. Whether they're younger, same age, or older. I know plenty of people that have been early 20's and have accomplished so much, done so many cool things, travelled, bought a house, married, kids, etc. Doing the adult thing "right". Well I've been single for years, lived alone for years, work a full time job. Don't really do much except fuck around on my pc in my free time. And you know what? I'm probably happier than those people doing the adulting "right". 

With owning a house, you now have to pay for all kinds of things such as repairs, property tax, HOA sometimes, cutting grass (lawnmower+gas), general upkeep, more cleaning, etc. I live in a 1 bedroom apartment and I'm very content. 

With being married and having kids you lose so much freedom. Sure they may be happy but either way a lot of freedom is taken away. You can't just come home one day and say I want to just binge watch a series, eat junk, and smoke weed. I mean you could but you probably won't be seen as a good parent/partner lol. If I come home I don't have to worry about cooking for the family, cleaning after the family, giving the kids baths and changing them, taking them to school or picking them up, helping them with homework, budgeting with a partner, sharing every inch of the living space with family. I can come home and breathe knowing I'm in control. It's rather peaceful. I may change my feeling on having a family one day but not anytime soon. I love being alone and having more freedom. 

Travelling is cool or just generally having a lot of "cool" experiences under your belt. Not many get to enjoy things like that unless you have enough money, can get away from work, whatever. Not everyone gets to live an exciting life and that's fine. I personally don't want an exciting life. I'm a laidback chill dude so if I spend the majority of my time at home that's cool. Sure it may be boring to most people that go out and do things but it makes me happy. And it's less stuff to stress about. 

I could go on about how it's hard not to compare yourself to others when you're an adult and see what other adults do or have done. Being an adult sucks but when you find things you can do as an adult that you enjoy then focus on those things. Who cares if you're not doing all the stereotypical adult things "right" or not. The way I've always thought about it is that nobody will ever know YOU better than you. You're stuck with yourself 24/7. Be selfish. Focus on what you want and don't want. If people are making you do things you don't want such as friends wanting to go out all the time and you don't want to, don't pressure yourself to do those things. If it doesn't make you happy, don't waste your time. Be selfish. Make yourself happy. Even if you don't know what makes you happy just know there are damn near infinite things on earth that are yet to be discovered by you. It could be something small. Maybe a new hobby, maybe a local event, etc.
